title: Traffic Valve Ramp with Shadow Probing and Failover Policy
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Design and implement a configurable 'traffic valve' primitive for model rollouts that combines staged traffic ramps, intermittent shadow probing, A/B split orchestration, and deterministic auto-rollback/failover behavior. The valve should be expressible in our rollout DSL and compile to runtime-safe policies: step schedules (timed or metric-triggered), fractional traffic splits, shadow probe waves (sampled duplicated requests), and multi-tier guardrails (latency, error, quality regressions). Deliverables: 1) rollout DSL extension for valve constructs; 2) runtime policy compiler that emits safe traffic controllers and fallbacks; 3) e2e simulation harness for validating safety curves; 4) operator-facing Console UI for observing valve state and initiating manual interventions.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: Aligning scope with Product. Key constraints: must support both hosted and dedicated, runtime must avoid head-of-line blocking, shadow probes must be low-cost and sampled, and rollback must be instant but safe for in-flight requests.

2025-02-13 - Architecture sync: Decided to model the valve as a finite-state controller with explicit states: Idle -> Ramp -> Probe -> Steady -> Rollback -> Failover. Each transition can be triggered by time OR metric predicates (percentile latency, p50-p99 delta, error rate, model-quality regression score).

2025-02-15 - Trade-off note: Strong hysteresis recommended on metric triggers to reduce flapping; we added exponential decay windows and 'grace-sample' counters so short blips don't trigger rollback. This increases complexity but reduces false positives significantly based on historical traces.

2025-02-17 - Design review (PM/Design/Eng): UX wants a single slider for quick ramps plus an advanced panel for step schedules. Action: add 'quickRamp' convenience that maps to {0->5%->20%->100%} over configurable durations.

2025-02-19 - Implementation update: DSL grammar pr opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4127. Prototype compiler emits runtime JSON with explicit token-bucket controllers per variant and a shadow-sampler policy for duplicated requests.

2025-02-21 - Testing: Ran simulation harness against historical traffic traces (synthesized from infra logs). Observed one false rollback due to correlated upstream dependency outage; added dependency-aware gating to avoid rolling back model for infra-induced errors.

2025-02-24 - Security review: Confirmed shadow traffic encryption and KMS usage for private deployments. Security asked for opt-in clear text suppression for PII-heavy requests; we've added a per-route masking flag.

2025-02-26 - Next steps: Stabilize compiler, add per-slice rollout (by cohort header), integrate Console timeline visualization, and prepare runtime Canary policy e2e tests. Beta plan targets selected Dedicated customers in April.
